title: Banners Gather at Bannerfall
text:
Bannerfall filled before the first Ledger bell.

Ranked clans occupied stone terraces according to position. Hearth delegates stood below them with tribute records, winter petitions and grievances strong enough to risk speaking upward. Physicians claimed white-cloth lanes no declared fighter could obstruct. Merchants carried the supplies every banner publicly pretended not to need.

At the basin’s center stood four seals.

Veyrhald’s Gate Seal could open southern military ports for a recognized foreign campaign. Dravaryn, Skeldran and Eirholt held Great Banner seals proving conquest, pursuit and survival. A war claim needed the Gate Seal and at least two Great Banners before Isgard would treat it as collective action rather than private raiding.

The Ledger Reading made rank practical. Higher banners received road priority, tribute shares, larger hunting rights and authority to sponsor foreign charters. Rank Four would make Duskvein a Great Banner and place its poison system inside southern governance.

Sera entered with the Rimeford clerks and watched where people moved when bells changed.

Rhen watched the five covered platforms guarded at opposite edges of the central court. For the first time, every cage stood within the reach of one field.

[[speaker:sera]]“Can you reach all five?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Can you heal them yet?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“No.”

The answer remained the same. The opportunity did not.

Around them, twelve armies arranged themselves beneath banners. Forty Quiet Hands disappeared into the work holding those armies together.

Winter Reckoning began as law, trade and memory.

Duskvein intended to turn it into permission for war.

title: Duskvein Brings Five Living Trophies
text:
Mareth Duskvein unveiled the Five Dukes one cage at a time.

The Keeper of the Last Pulse wore unadorned grey and listened to each captive’s circulation while Oren recited titles. World Six through Ten. Wuyue’s compact expedition. Defeated alive by one Duskvein hunting cohort.

The crowd saw broken bodies.

Sera saw work.

Ilyra sagged against her restraints while secretly holding two poison cycles apart. Mo let one torn paper edge cling beneath his platform. Arin’s left hand rested against the weakened chain link. Luo coughed at exact intervals marking the Wardens. Yun breathed the seven-venom sequence where Seo could hear it.

Each used the display to place evidence in reach.

[[speaker:mareth]]“Duskvein has opened the first road into Wuyue. Rank Four recognizes value already proven.”

Dravaryn soldiers struck spear shafts against stone. Duskvein dependents followed after checking which officers watched. Eirholt’s section remained silent.

Mareth moved between the cages touching no one. His basin lattice read their pulses through prepared ground. Peak Sovereign pressure approached Paragon without becoming a Domain; every hidden anchor strengthened it by borrowing from poisoned bodies.

Rhen’s expression did not change. Sera felt his hand close once beneath his sleeve.

The Five Dukes looked thoroughly defeated because they were.

They also entered Bannerfall carrying a synchronized case against the people displaying them.

Duskvein had brought five living trophies.

It had failed to notice that all five were still fighting.

title: The First Banner Does Not Applaud
text:
Tor Veyrhald did not strike his spear against stone.

The Iron Witness sat beneath the First Banner’s black-and-silver cloth, weathered face turned toward Mareth. High Sovereign pressure rested inside his posture without entering the court.

He was not among Veyrhald’s strongest three.

That fact travelled through the foreign observers more sharply than any display. Southern Isgard’s first-ranked clan had sent a man capable of deciding ordinary wars and still considered him an envoy rather than its summit.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“You request the Gate Seal.”

[[speaker:mareth]]“Duskvein has satisfied foreign value and collective depth.”

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“You have satisfied capture.”

Tor Veyrhald did not defend Wuyue. He asked whether the victory strengthened Isgard or manufactured retaliation for one guild’s advancement. A Gate Seal could not be awarded because captives existed; Duskvein had to prove its evidence, sponsorship and dependent testimony survived challenge.

Oren demanded immediate recognition.

Tor Veyrhald placed the Gate Seal facedown.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“Evidence first.”

The refusal created no alliance. If Duskvein proved its case, the Iron Witness might open the ports himself.

But law now possessed a narrow interval.

Sera had until the seal turned faceup to break the claim without fighting the whole basin.

title: Eirholt’s Physician Counts the Lies
text:
Eira Eirholt counted treatment gaps.

The Winter Physician was broad-shouldered, frost-burned and uninterested in Oren’s speeches. She compared Duskvein’s public care record with pulse readings taken whenever white-cloth law allowed her near the cages.

Five listed treatments had never occurred. Three antidote doses were weaker than claimed. Luo’s injuries proved he had been treating hunters while denied equivalent care. Ilyra’s second poison cycle did not appear anywhere in the Guild record.

Seo Dabin passed Eira one discarded vial through an infirmary waste count. Yun’s breathing supplied the ratio inside it.

Eira understood.

[[speaker:eira]]“Your captives regulate your prison.”

[[speaker:oren]]“They receive continuous treatment.”

[[speaker:eira]]“They provide it.”

Medical neutrality protected treatment intervals, truthful injury reporting and physicians acting without political punishment. Duskvein had converted all three into pressure. Its antidote quotas controlled Hearth testimony. Its records concealed deliberate suffering. Its captives were simultaneously patients and machinery.

Eira placed Eirholt’s white seal against the Rank Four petition.

[[speaker:eira]]“Survival purchased through manufactured dependence is not medical value.”

The fourth-ranked banner did not oppose Duskvein merely to keep rank. Its own legitimacy depended upon treatment remaining something stronger clans could not quietly turn into ownership.

One Great Banner seal was now closed.

title: Sera Enters Without a Banner
text:
Sera entered the central court carrying one medicine case.

Rhen carried the other two.

[[speaker:rhen]]“The division remains unequal.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You packed them.”

Their disagreement followed them past twelve armies and made several warriors dismiss the pair as married physicians choosing a terrible moment to argue.

Oren recognized her first. Older intelligence officials followed. The name Pale Orchid moved through the court more slowly than fear, because most of Isgard knew the legend and not the face.

[[speaker:oren]]“Sera of Wuyue.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Sera is sufficient.”

She carried no Domain banner, public rank or military seal. Peak Sovereign strength remained folded beneath **Veiled Moon**, present without demanding recognition.

[[speaker:mareth]]“You challenge Duskvein’s rank?”

[[speaker:sera]]“I challenge your evidence.”

Sera named the poisoned testimony, the false pursuit record and the prison functions hidden from Eirholt. She did not claim the Five Dukes belonged to her, Wuyue or The Quaint Teahouse.

[[speaker:sera]]“Capturing people proves you prepared well. Converting their pain into a charter proves only what your campaign requires others to endure.”

Mareth invited her to settle the matter through a declared contest.

Sera refused.

[[speaker:sera]]“The Ledger is on trial. Not my fist.”

She entered Bannerfall without a banner and forced every ranked clan to decide whether Duskvein’s method could become the law governing them next.

title: Forty Hands Among Twelve Armies
text:
The Quiet Hands never formed a line.

Cell Three entered infirmaries. Cell Five entered kitchens and tribute offices. Iron specialists repaired stands built over poison anchors. Wayfinders learned drains, snow channels and every gate whose closure could turn Bannerfall into a prison.

To the twelve armies, they were clerks, cooks, stable workers, physicians and hired labor. No uniform joined them.

Each ordinary position gave Sera one option.

A kitchen worker could prevent poisoned smoke entering civilian quarters. A clerk could preserve testimony before Oren altered it. A stable hand could open evacuation carts. A Spring specialist could keep one Hearth witness alive long enough to speak.

Tae remained beyond the basin, holding the cage distances in awareness without announcing a High Sovereign. Lei and Rui approached separately through the southern roads. Rhen stayed beside Sera because every captive now stood within his reach and none could yet survive treatment.

Sera touched no weapon.

She moved one cup, folded one cloth and changed which gate received grain. Forty people adjusted without a visible order.

Duskvein had brought a Guild into Bannerfall.

Sera had placed a hand inside everything the Guild assumed was background.

title: The Ledger Can Be Poisoned
text:
Mei Rulan proved the testimony had a dosage schedule.

Ashpine growers entered under Eirholt’s white cloth carrying antidote tokens reduced after they questioned Duskvein quotas. Rimeford records showed the same pattern across four Hearths. Neris’s ledger linked medicine priority directly to political support.

Oren called the records forgeries.

Mei placed his service account beside the original freight books. He had counted dependent medicine as voluntary tribute and omitted every allocation suspended after dissent.

[[speaker:rulan]]“The Ledger records loyalty.”

[[speaker:oren]]“Correct.”

[[speaker:rulan]]“Then it must distinguish loyalty from withdrawal sickness.”

Raska Dravaryn rose beneath the Rank Two banner. The Crimson Marshal wore layered red armor and carried enough High Sovereign pressure to silence the terrace without releasing it.

Dravaryn wanted Wuyue opened. Its armies had also relied upon Duskvein medicine for years. Raska would not let those facts turn forged proof into honor.

[[speaker:raska]]“Our provisional conquest seal is suspended.”

Mareth accused Sera of manipulating Hearth weakness.

[[speaker:sera]]“I gave them another physician.”

The issue no longer belonged to Wuyue. If Duskvein could poison testimony into loyalty, every Banner rank could be purchased through controlled dependence.

The Ledger itself had become the patient.

title: A Paper Bird Reaches the Field
text:
Mo’s paper bird crossed Bannerfall beneath a tribute cart.

It reached the central field as Oren presented Skeldran’s seal record. The bird unfolded against Sera’s boot, its creases carrying the prisoners’ synchronized testimony: seven venoms, five regulator roles, false harbor turns and one route discrepancy only a Skeldran Huntmaster could verify.

A horn sounded at the southern gate.

Varok entered with surviving hunters and Wuyue’s copied evidence. His armor remained broken where Huo had stopped one palm. He knelt to no Wuyue representative. He faced Skeldran’s own terrace.

[[speaker:varok]]“The pursuit record is false.”

Oren challenged the claim. Varok recited the impossible flood route, the repeated pressure error and the markers Huo had returned intact. Skeldran’s record keepers confirmed each contradiction.

The Rank Three banner withdrew its pursuit seal.

Mo’s bird moved once more, pointing toward the cages. Yun changed her breathing. Luo answered through pulse. Arin touched the prepared link. Ilyra opened her eyes.

Five separate prisoners delivered one testimony in front of Isgard.

Duskvein could no longer call the evidence foreign rumor.

title: Ilyra Challenges Her Own Price
text:
Ilyra stood by using both chains.

The effort tore one poison cycle through her left palm. She remained upright until the court looked at her rather than Mareth.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“Duskvein defeated us.”

The admission quieted every friendly argument.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“They prepared better. They separated five Dukes, used civilians correctly and prevented our strength from becoming escape.”

Mareth smiled.

Ilyra continued.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“That proves one cohort can capture five people inside a prepared harbor. It does not prove Duskvein can conquer Wuyue after warning it.”

She named the rotation cost, the Wardens required, the poisoned terrain and the living regulators holding the victory together. Duskvein had won through precision. Its public claim inflated that precision into continental certainty.

Then Ilyra looked at Sera.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“I am not their trophy.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“I am not yours to retrieve because Wuyue owns me.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“Bring us out because we choose to leave.”

[[speaker:sera]]“That is the mission.”

The rescue became consent spoken before the entire Ledger.

Ilyra challenged both the captor’s price and any ally tempted to answer ownership with another form of possession.

title: The Seventh Banner Calls for Wuyue
text:
Mareth lost Rank Four before he abandoned law.

Eirholt opposed. Dravaryn suspended. Skeldran withdrew. Veyrhald’s Gate Seal remained facedown.

The Keeper of the Last Pulse touched the court floor.

Hidden poison anchors answered across Bannerfall. Needles rose inside snow channels. Hearth smoke turned grey. Antidote-dependent soldiers felt their hearts tighten together. Mareth’s basin lattice stopped resembling a political claim and became the threat underneath it.

[[speaker:mareth]]“Turn the seals.”

Tor Veyrhald kept the Gate Seal facedown.

[[speaker:tor_veyrhald]]“A seal taken from a poisoned hand records nothing.”

Mareth increased the pressure. Civilians fell. Quiet Hands began the evacuation routes Sera had prepared. Tae’s presence entered the basin edge but did not strike. Sera assigned fronts and kept lethal authority closed while patients remained inside every hostile formation.

When the seals still did not turn, Mareth looked toward the execution court.

[[speaker:mareth]]“Garran. Prove submission.”

The Iron Leech entered between the five cages. High Sovereign pressure rolled from his body through iron rings tied to the prison lattice. He selected Ilyra first because her dual meridians had resisted every transfer.

[[speaker:garran]]“The others will learn through you.”

Rhen took one step.

Sera caught his hand. Not to stop him forever. To hold the final instant before action became safe.

Winter Reckoning ended without a lawful rank.

Duskvein called for Wuyue through pain instead.
